title: Object gluing with prescribed derived transition
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U,V$ opens with $U\cup V=X$, and fix derived categories of module sheaves on $X,U,V,W=U\cap V$ in morphism universe $w$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Restriction to an open is overFunctor followed by overEquiv; restriction from $U$ or $V$ to $W$ is the inverse open equivalence, overMap, then overEquiv for $W$. For $A\in D(\mathcal O_U)$, $B\in D(\mathcal O_V)$ and $c:A|_W\cong B|_W$, there exist $F\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, $i_U:F|_U\cong A$ and $i_V:F|_V\cong B$ such that $i_V|_W=c\circ i_U|_W$, using the canonical iterated-restriction comparisons. This assertion has no morphism-lifting clause.

proof.text: Let j_U, j_V, j_W be the open immersions of U, V and W=U\cap V into X, with derived direct images Rj_{U,*}, Rj_{V,*}, Rj_{W,*} as in [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open]. Form the morphism Rj_{U,*}A\oplus Rj_{V,*}B\to Rj_{W,*}(B|_W) whose V component is minus the restriction map and whose U component is the restriction map Rj_{U,*}A\to Rj_{W,*}(A|_W) followed by Rj_{W,*}c. By the triangulated structure of the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] (applied to the abelian category of \mathcal O_X-modules) it sits in a distinguished triangle F\to Rj_{U,*}A\oplus Rj_{V,*}B\to Rj_{W,*}(B|_W)\to F[1]; this defines F.

Restrict the triangle to U. By [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] (Tag 08FE) applied to f=j_V and the open U (so f^{-1}U=W and g=j:W\to U), to f=j_W and U (g=j), and to f=j_U and U (g=\mathrm{id}_U), the restriction to U of the V pushforward and of the W pushforward are both canonically Rj_*(B|_W), and the restriction of the U pushforward is A. Under these identifications, the second arrow is the difference of the map induced by c and the identity on the pushforward from U∩V, so its projection to the second summand is an isomorphism and has a section. The cone triangle of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] for a morphism with such a section is isomorphic to the triangle with first term A; hence F|_U≅A. Restricting to V gives F|_V≅B by the same displayed split-cone calculation with the two summands interchanged. Under these identifications, the two component maps on U∩V are c and the identity, so the transition isomorphism is c.

theorem derived_open_gluing_objects
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U V : X.Opens) (hcover : U ⊔ V = ⊤)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    (A : schemeDerivedCategory U.toScheme) (B : schemeDerivedCategory V.toScheme)
    (c : (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_left) ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V))).mapDerivedCategory.obj A ≅
      (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_right) ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V))).mapDerivedCategory.obj B) :
    ∃ (F : schemeDerivedCategory X)
      (iU : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory.obj F ≅ A)
      (iV : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) V ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V)).mapDerivedCategory.obj F ≅ B),
      ((Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso
          (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U))
          (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_left) ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V)))).symm ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso
          (Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerLeft
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U)
            ((Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
              Functor.isoWhiskerRight (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U).unitIso.symm _ ≪≫
                Functor.leftUnitor _) ≪≫
          (Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctorMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_left))
            (Equivalence.functor
              (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
              (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
              (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V))))).inv.app F ≫
        (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_left) ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V))).mapDerivedCategory.map iU.hom ≫ c.hom =
      ((Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso
          (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) V ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V))
          (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_right) ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V)))).symm ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso
          (Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerLeft
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) V)
            ((Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
              Functor.isoWhiskerRight (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V).unitIso.symm _ ≪≫
                Functor.leftUnitor _) ≪≫
          (Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctorMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_right))
            (Equivalence.functor
              (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
              (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
              (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V))))).inv.app F ≫
        (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings V.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv V) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE inf_le_right) ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over (U ⊓ V)))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (U ⊓ V).toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv (U ⊓ V))).mapDerivedCategory.map iV.hom
